dedupe_keys.name: odheatmap open data district heating feasibility model

description: ODHeatMap estimates building heat demand and district-heating potential from open geographic data. Diana Moreno at Aalborg University publishes the model as a notebook with four documented stages: retrieve building footprints, estimate building-envelope surface area, estimate heat demand and aggregate district-heating potential to a grid. The workflow targets places where detailed local heat-demand data are unavailable. It is intended for global application where suitable inputs exist, but the inspected README does not specify a default grid size, reference year or update interval. Outputs are written as GeoPackage files. The code is freely available through GitHub under MIT; the licence file separately lists ODbL, Copernicus terms and CC BY 4.0 for different input sources. Users must retain those data-specific conditions. Building geometry and estimated demand are screening inputs, not verified heat-meter observations or a hydraulic pipe model. Simulation uses include district-heating capacity planning and identifying candidate service areas. The model relates to data-hotmaps-building-stock-and-heat-density-maps and data-openstreetmap. Its notebook was not executed, so geographic completeness and the accuracy of derived demand were not independently tested.
